quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F: 2025 sales were $61,352 million (2024: $62,441 million) - North America $12,335 million, Brazil $11,172 million, Europe $28,793 million, Sustainable Solutions $10,501 million, Mining $3,232 million (segment sales before eliminations); operating income was $3,628 million (2024: $3,310 million) - North America $2,205 million, Brazil $608 million, Europe $522 million, Sustainable Solutions $142 million, Mining $789 million; capital expenditures were $4,337 million.

ArcelorMittal 20-F: in 2025 it produced 55.6 million tonnes of crude steel (41.2 million tonnes via BOF, 14.4 million tonnes via EAF) against achievable capacity of 74.6 million tonnes (76.7 million tonnes in 2024); steel shipments were 54.0 million tonnes (54.3 million tonnes in 2024); iron ore reserves were estimated at 3,728 million tonnes run of mine; it had 125,554 FTE employees at year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: crude steel 55.6 million tonnes; capacity 74.6 million tonnes; shipments 54.0 million tonnes

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F: 2026 capital expenditures are expected at $4.5 to 5.0 billion, of which $1.4 to $1.8 billion strategic growth capex and approximately $0.3 billion decarbonization projects; 2025 strategic growth capex was $1.1 billion, with the Liberia expansion, the Calvert EAF and electrical steels facility and Mardyck electrical steels taking 42%, 22% and 13% of it.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex $4.5 to 5.0 billion; strategic growth $1.4 to $1.8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F (Calvert): on June 18, 2025 ArcelorMittal acquired Nippon Steel's 50% stake in AMNS Calvert and took control of the facility (hot strip mill 5.3 million tonnes, cold rolling 3.6 million tonnes, finishing 2.1 million tonnes); its new 1.5 million tonnes EAF and caster (investment over $1 billion) produced its first heat on June 14, 2025; the 1.5 million tonnes per year slab agreement with Cleveland-Cliffs expired on December 9, 2025, replaced in part by a new seven-year domestic slab supply agreement with Nippon Steel averaging 750,000 tonnes per year; a NOES facility of up to 150,000 tonnes per year is planned with estimated net capex raised to $1.3 billion (previously $0.9 billion, net of $0.3 billion of public support) and production from the second half of 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Calvert EAF 1.5 million tonnes; NOES up to 150,000 tonnes; net capex $1.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F: it is expanding electrical steel capacity for e-mobility, renewable energy and 'emerging areas like data centers', investing in 0.4 million tonnes of NOES in the U.S. and EU by 2028 (Mardyck, France: 155 thousand tonnes per year NOES, reversing mill in the second half of 2026 and annealing and pickling line in the first half of 2027).
quarterly_data.figure: 0.4 million tonnes of NOES by 2028; Mardyck 155 thousand tonnes

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F (France): in February 2026 the company confirmed construction of a 2-million-tonne EAF in Dunkirk, a strategic investment of approximately EUR 1.3 billion with start-up scheduled for 2029; in December 2025 it signed an agreement with EDF to secure long-term low-carbon electricity for its French sites, and the 18-year nuclear power production allocation contract with EDF signed on December 26, 2025 raised its raw-material and energy purchase commitments by $5.6 billion (total $17,115 million at year-end 2025 vs $10,082 million).
quarterly_data.figure: Dunkirk EAF 2 million tonnes, approximately EUR 1.3 billion; purchase commitments $17,115 million

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F (renewables): 1.6GW of renewable capacity (equity share) is commissioned (India 1GW, Brazil 0.6GW, Argentina 0.1GW) and a further 1.2GW is under development for commissioning by 2028; the 975 MW Andhra Pradesh solar and wind project ($0.7 billion) began supplying AMNS India in May 2025, and three new India projects announced on December 22, 2025 (1GW, capex $0.9 billion) will take its global renewable capacity to 3.3GW.

ArcelorMittal 20-F (Liberia): approximately 10 million tonnes were shipped in 2025, with a 20 million tonnes shipment target in 2026; the Phase 2 project capex was revised to $1.8 billion (previously $1.4 billion) for 20 million tonnes per annum of shipment capacity, a phased expansion to 30 million tonnes per annum is under study, and the Mineral Development Agreement was extended to 2050 (amendment ratified January 29, 2026).
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 10 million tonnes shipped in 2025; capex $1.8 billion; 30 million tonnes under study

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F (AMNS India, 60/40 joint venture with Nippon Steel): achievable crude steel capacity of 8.8 million tonnes per annum; phase 1 expansion capex of approximately $7.7 billion aims to raise Hazira production to 15 million tonnes of rolled products by the second half of 2026; plans are under development for an 8.2 million tonnes greenfield integrated plant in Andhra Pradesh toward a 40 million tonnes per annum target.
quarterly_data.figure: 8.8 million tonnes capacity; $7.7 billion phase 1; 15 million tonnes by H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 20-F (portfolio changes): it completed the acquisition of a 28.4% stake in the associate Vallourec in August 2024 (27.8% at December 31, 2025, equity-method associate); acquired an 89.69% interest in Tekno S.A. (coil coating, Brazil) on November 3, 2025 and the remaining 49% of the Perfilor joint venture, gaining control; and raised its stake in ArcelorMittal Tailored Blanks Americas from 80% to 90% with control on April 1, 2025.
ArcelorMittal 20-F (Ukraine): ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih ran its open pit mines and steel facilities at 73% and 35% capacity, respectively, in 2025.
